qualifications_or_emphasis: Emphasis of Matter: Implementation of approved resolution plan under Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (Note No. 29). The company was under CIRP and resolution plan was approved by NCLT, Mumbai Bench vide order dated February 11, 2025.

Emphasis of Matter: Company's ability to continue as a going concern (Note No. 30). The Company has not carried out regular business operations and its net worth has been eroded, which may cast significant doubt on its ability to continue as a going concern. However, pursuant to the Resolution Plan approved by the NCLT, the Company has been taken over by new promoters and management, who intend to revive the operations and introduce new business opportunities. Accordingly, the financial statements have been prepared on a going concern basis.

outlook.statement: The Board is confident that the Company will continue as a going concern for the foreseeable future, including the next 12 months and beyond. The management is committed to executing the business plan and delivering long-term value to shareholders, employees, and other stakeholders.
outlook.period: foreseeable future, including the next 12 months and beyond

outlook.statement: Global steel demand is projected to grow by 1.5% in 2026, reaching ~1,722 million tonnes. After three consecutive years of decline, steel demand is expected to recover globally (excluding China) in 2026. A stable global economic outlook, coupled with improving financing conditions and real income growth in major economies, is expected to support recovery in private consumption and investments before the tariff impositions. Additionally, a significant recovery in residential construction is also anticipated from 2026 onward, supported by easing financing conditions. However, the tariffs imposed by US administration and reciprocal tariffs by countries has led to increased uncertainty in demand-supply balance and continues to be a major risk to the steel industry.
The Directors are making continuous efforts to revive the business activities of the Company and are optimistic about improving its performance.
The Company has been taken over by new promoters and management to revive operations and bring new business opportunities.

litigation: The Company underwent Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, pursuant to which a Resolution Plan was approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT).
According to the information provided by the management, there is no pending litigation which may impact the financial position of the Company.
Resolution plan approved by the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench (NCLT) vide its Order dated 11 February 2025 under the provisions of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016

Pursuant to an application filed under Section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (IBC), the Hon'ble National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), Mumbai Bench, vide its order dated 08 December 2023 in C.P. No. 811/2023, admitted the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) of the Company.
risks: Susceptibility to cyclicality associated with the steel industry and availability of key raw materials
Demand for steel is sensitive to trends in key end-use industries, such as automobiles, infrastructure, construction and consumer durables
Steel business would continue to be affected by developments impacting the demand-supply scenario & price fluctuations of steels in both the global and domestic markets
Rising inflation can impact consumption and lead to fiscal tightening increasing the cost of borrowings affecting investments
Intensification of geopolitical tension in Europe can disrupt the whole market dynamics
Tariffs imposed by US administration and reciprocal tariffs by countries has led to increased uncertainty in demand-supply balance and continues to be a major risk to the steel industry
